verdicts.note: Girls' school plus self-references as a woman ('cos you're a woman'); clearly female.
'I went to a girls' school' — explicit single-sex secondary school.
Industrial Design & Technology student; Design & Technology department fits.
Choosing 'second year' options now and applying for placement fits Year 2, but 'when I was in the second year' elsewhere is ambiguous; downgrade.
Chose it because 'making things... quite interesting'; supports interesting-work draw.
Quote about 'big variety of things' is in a course-range/prospects context, not stated as a reason it appealed; thin and overlaps with variety var.
Having done A-level Physics does not establish she was GOOD at maths/science; she says she didn't expect to pursue it and leans creative/anti-technical. Quote does not support the item.
Dad businessman, mum administration; no family in industry; disagree is correct.
Prefers creative over technical side; supports disagree that interests are technical.
A school careers TEST suggested 'designer'; mild, not an advisor actively 'encouraging' — weak support for agree.
'The teacher kind of encouraged it... don't be discouraged'; clear teacher encouragement.
Supportive but 'wouldn't say they've influenced me'; mum doesn't like design — disagree correct.
Parents supportive but did not encourage/influence; disagree fits father.
Reports encouragement and 'don't be discouraged'; no account of anyone discouraging her — no is correct.
'a lot harder than I thought... emphasis on technology'; curriculum harder than expected.
'Yeah, yeah definitely' to being pleased she chose the course.
Assistant 'known for helping girls out more than boys' with a concrete example; agree well supported.
Group work seen as developing teamwork/working-with-others; supports interpersonal-skills agree.
Chosen quote ('extra helpful') is in the SCHOOL-teacher context and one course lecturer was 'not particularly helpful'; mixed — downgrade.
Both personal tutors 'really friendly, very helpful'; satisfied is well supported.
'I do actually... we've all been helpful, friendly, willing to work'; satisfied with group work.
Prefers the creative/design side; supports satisfaction with design work.

Quote 'making things... interesting' is from her school taster, not satisfaction with course practical work; on the course she found technical/hands-on bits hard and dropped mechanics. Does not support the item.
'big variety of things' — positive about variety of subjects; satisfied fits.
'I've applied... to go on a placement course'; intends placement — yes.
'a really good way of getting work experience' — first/primary reason; strongly agree defensible.
Names 'Money (laughs)' first, but elsewhere says pay is 'a bonus' and she 'hasn't worried about pay' — ambivalent; agree is thin, downgrade.
'find something I really enjoy... know what I want to go for after I graduate'; strongly agree supported.
'see how design works in industry... completely different to designing on a course'; strongly agree supported.
'more organised within yourself, making sure you do things'; personal development agree supported.
'a year's experience would be really good' is generic value of experience, not explicitly about getting a job; thin — downgrade.
'scared you'd lose some skills... forget everything' — fear of returning rusty; reasonably matches difficulty getting back after a break.
She CHOSE to restrict to local and found a house; quote is a location preference/deterrent, not 'could not find one in a suitable location' — only loosely fits; downgrade.
'most of them I'm not interested in... really far away or really technical'; many did not appeal.
'broad range of design', not technical/industrial; design work fits.
'haven't worried too much about pay... nice to get paid'; low-priority but not dismissed — neither important nor unimportant is defensible.
'definitely around [university area]... I've restricted myself to that'; location important.
Drawn to 'creative... relaxed... not very formal'; work environment matters — important.
Quote is about placement pay, not the field-choice draw, but substantively she chose for creativity not salary; disagree holds, though quote is off-context — downgrade.
Quote reports what OTHER 3rd years said about avoiding placement; it is not her own view on further study, which the interview never probes. Does not support a 'no'.
